notes: Guided launch interview question bank (doc 03). The canonical bank shared with the legacy interview, Skill 71 and Skill 83 is shared-utils/client_intake/question-bank.json (each question here maps to a canonical id through its legacy_ids); answers live in one answers file, see intake/INTAKE.md. One focused question per turn; at most three short choices including the client's own answer. Conditions are evaluated against the answer ledger; a question whose condition fails is skipped, never asked. Field states: provided | verified_existing | recommended_unapproved | approved_recommendation | unknown | not_applicable. Blank is not not_applicable.

choices: A: Recommend a plan for me (use what is known, ask only what is missing, let them review)
B: Guide me through each decision (explain options, help them choose)
C: I already have a plan (help act, flag anything important missed)
questions.prompt: What is the best way for me to help you with your launch?
questions.reason: It sets how much I suggest and how much I ask. You can change this preference later. Anything I recommend is a proposal for your review - never a silent decision, and never approval for spending.

choice_explanations.A: Recommend a plan for me (use what is: I use what you have already told me, ask only for what is missing, and put the plan in front of you to review before anything is built.
choice_explanations.B: Guide me through each decision (expla: I explain each decision in plain language, walk the options with you, and help you choose.
choice_explanations.C: I already have a plan (help act, flag: You bring the plan; I help you act on it and flag anything important it misses.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A, B and C are all good answers. Pick the one that fits how you want to work today.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.prompt: What is the business outcome you want from this launch? One sentence is plenty.
questions.reason: Every page and message serves this outcome, and it keeps the plan honest about what a launch can realistically do.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Think about what would make this launch worth it. A rough answer is fine.
examples: Fill all 12 seats in my group program before the end of November.
Get 30 new sign-ups for my workshop.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.prompt: What is making that hard right now?
questions.reason: The page and the follow-up answer your real obstacle instead of a guess.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Name the biggest obstacle first; we can cover the rest later.
examples: People visit my page but never book a call.
My list is small and I do not know how to reach new people.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.prompt: What are you offering? A rough sentence, a link, or pasted notes are all fine.
questions.reason: The main offer and its buyer anchor every later choice.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Say what it is in your own words. The buyer comes next - one question at a time.
examples: A 6-week group program that helps new coaches get their first 10 paying clients.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.prompt: Who is it for? A rough description of the people you want to reach is plenty.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me

examples: New coaches who have never had a paying client.
Busy parents planning a first marathon.

questions.prompt: Do you have any real results, stories, or kind words from buyers we may use? Paste or link them, or say none yet.
questions.reason: Proof must be real and attributed; missing proof is never invented.
questions.recommendation_rule: When none is supplied, mark proof not_applicable and plan a proof-free narrative; never fabricate testimonials.

choice_explanations.I have some to share: Real words from real buyers are the strongest proof. Paste or link whatever you have.
choice_explanations.Use my own story: Your own experience can carry the page instead of buyer quotes.
choice_explanations.None yet: That is completely fine. The page is built without testimonials - nothing is invented.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Proof must be real and attributed; missing proof is never invented.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

questions.prompt: Will buyers choose one offer, or choose between a few packages?
questions.reason: Decides whether a product selection page exists in the route.
questions.recommendation_rule: Two or more meaningfully different main packages described in Phase A -> recommend multiple_options; one offer -> single_simple. Different payment schedules alone do not require a selection page.

choice_explanations.One offer: Everyone buys the same thing - the simplest, clearest funnel.
choice_explanations.A few packages: Buyers pick between clearly different options.
choice_explanations.Help me decide: I recommend the simplest shape that serves your plan.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Decides whether a product selection page exists in the route.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

choices: Suggest one for me to review
questions.prompt: Do you already have a price for it, or should I suggest a starting price for you to review?
questions.reason: A price is a commercial fact; a suggestion is a proposal, never a proven optimum.
questions.recommendation_rule: A suggested price must state its rationale from known delivery cost, scope and supplied market context, and stays recommended_unapproved until the plan is approved. Unknown price is recorded unknown - never zero.

choice_explanations.I have a price: Your price is a fact we can build on.
choice_explanations.Suggest one for me to review: I suggest a starting price with my reasoning; it stays a proposal until you approve it.
choice_explanations.It is free: A free offer still needs a clear page and follow-up.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: A price is a commercial fact; a suggestion is a proposal, never a proven optimum.
actions: Recommend something using what you already know about my business.

choice_explanations.Yes, I have one: You already have a small add-on in mind.
choice_explanations.Recommend one: I suggest one only if it genuinely helps them use what they bought.
choice_explanations.No add-on: A clean checkout with nothing extra is a good choice.

questions.prompt: After they buy, is there a useful upgrade or extra product you want to offer?
questions.reason: Upsell 1 must add incremental value, never repeat the purchase.
questions.recommendation_rule: Recommend U1 only from a distinct second product in supplied facts; name the assumption and confirm it is actually deliverable.

choice_explanations.Yes, I have one: You have a next step ready for people who want more.
choice_explanations.Recommend one: Only from what you have told me, and only if you can deliver it.
choice_explanations.No upgrade: Keeping the funnel to the main offer is often the simplest, strongest choice.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: Upsell 1 must add incremental value, never repeat the purchase.

questions.prompt: If they pass on that upgrade, is there a smaller version or an easier way to buy it?
questions.reason: The downsell is a changed scope or changed terms - a lower installment is not a lower total price.
questions.recommendation_rule: If no good alternative exists in supplied facts, recommend no downsell rather than inventing one.

choice_explanations.Yes, a smaller version: A lighter version of the upgrade for people who pass.
choice_explanations.Yes, easier payments: The same upgrade on friendlier payment terms.
choice_explanations.No downsell: Their no is accepted - no second pitch.

help.label: I'm not sure, help me
help.explain: The downsell is a changed scope or changed terms - a lower installment is not a lower total price.

questions.recommendation_rule: Recommend U2 only from a distinct third product in supplied facts that does not duplicate the bump or a package inclusion.

choice_explanations.Yes, I have one: You have one more genuinely different product to offer.
choice_explanations.Recommend one: Only if your facts include a distinct third product - never a repeat.
choice_explanations.No second upsell: One extra offer is often plenty.
